question.worked_solution:
Let $y=\operatorname{cosh}⁡((x-2)^{2}).$ Since $x\ge 2,$ we have $y\ge 1.$

To find the inverse function, we swap $x$ and $y:$

$$
x=\operatorname{cosh}⁡((y-2)^{2}),
$$

where $x\ge 1$ and $y\ge 2.$

Next, we apply the definition of hyperbolic cosine:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{1}{2}\,({e}^{(y-2)^{2}}+{e}^{-(y-2)^{2}}) \\ 2x & ={e}^{(y-2)^{2}}+{e}^{-(y-2)^{2}} \\ 2x{e}^{(y-2)^{2}} & ={e}^{2(y-2)^{2}}+1\end{aligned}
$$

Bringing everything to the left-hand side, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{2(y-2)^{2}}-2x{e}^{(y-2)^{2}}+1 & =0 \\ ({e}^{(y-2)^{2}})^{2}-2x({e}^{(y-2)^{2}})+1 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $Y={e}^{(y-2)^{2}}.$ We can form a quadratic equation in $Y$ and solve it by completing the square, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{Y}^{2}-2xY+1 & =0 \\ (Y-x)^{2}-{x}^{2}+1 & =0 \\ (Y-x)^{2} & ={x}^{2}-1 \\ Y-x & =\pm \sqrt{{x}^{2}-1} \\ Y & =x\pm \sqrt{{x}^{2}-1} \\ {e}^{(y-2)^{2}} & =x\pm \sqrt{{x}^{2}-1} \\ (y-2)^{2} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x\pm \sqrt{{x}^{2}-1})\end{aligned}
$$

Note that for  $x\ge 1,$ we have $x-\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}\le 1$ and  $x+\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}\ge 1.$ Since the logarithm in the above equality must be positive, we reject the alternative with the negative sign. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-2)^{2} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}) \\ y-2 & =\pm \sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1})} \\ y & =2\pm \sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1})}\end{aligned}
$$

Since we want $y\ge 2,$ select the positive solution. Therefore,

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1})}+2.
$$
